headline: Brazil's press, Scotland's silence: 0-3 tells the true story
story: Brazil imposed themselves immediately, with an early goal inside seven minutes setting an ominous tone. Vinicius Júnior and his teammates pressed relentlessly—4.5 high-press phases against Scotland's meek 2.3—suffocating any Scottish rhythm. The second goal came just before halftime, delivered when Scotland's best hope of containment had already evaporated. By the hour mark, a third goal confirmed what the stats had already foretold: Scotland, in 4-2-3-1 formation, were simply outclassed. Possession (51-43) meant little when Brazil's defensive shape was impenetrable.

The xG gulf told the story: 3.78 to 0.69, a chasm. Scotland's sluggish ball recovery (23.3 seconds versus Brazil's 19.2) combined with Brazil's superior press to create a perfect storm of disruption. McTominay (7.0) and Ferguson (7.1) fought hard in midfield, but Brazil's coordinated pressing suffocated them. Scotland's Shankland, rated 6.9, barely posed a threat. Brazil's attacking trio—Júnior (8.8), Alisson (8.3), and Cunha (8.3)—simply played at another level. One clear miss at 81' (xG 0.88) briefly suggested vulnerability, but Brazil's dominance was too complete.

keyMoment.text: Brazil's second goal before halftime; the moment Scotland's slim hopes evaporated

home.verdict: Outpressed and ineffective; Brazil's dominance was inevitable given the tactical mismatch
points: Early vulnerability (7'): conceding so quickly stole any Scottish hope; resilient defending in opening 15 minutes was critical
Pressing intensity (2.3 vs 4.5 phases): Brazil's press suffocated Scotland; higher Scottish press might have disrupted Brazil's build-up
Ball recovery gap (23.3s vs 19.2s): slow recovery allowed Brazil's press to reset; quicker transitions were essential

away.verdict: Relentless press and early strikes: Brazil's tactical superiority proved overwhelming
points: Early strikes (7', 45+3): Brazil scored from high-xG chances (0.95, 0.77) before Scotland settled; early psychological advantage was decisive
Press domination (4.5 vs 2.3 phases): Brazil's relentless, coordinated press systematically dismantled Scotland's structure; this tactical dominance was decisive
Missed chance at 81' (xG 0.88): this slip would have cost most sides; Scotland's collapse meant Brazil's miss was consequence-free

statLine: Brazil generated 3.78 expected goals to Scotland's 0.69—a chasm that made the 3-0 scoreline almost merciful
